The test image shows a cross-section (end view) of a corn ear with:
- Tan/brown discolored kernels
- Grayish-white mycelium/fungal growth in the center and between kernels
- Small dark specks (possible pycnidia)
- Overall rotted appearance

This points to an ear rot. The white-gray mycelium with straw-colored kernels and dark specks suggests Diplodia ear rot. Let me confirm with the reference.

The reference images for Ear_rots_Diplodia show:
- Straw/tan-colored bleached kernels
- White mycelium growing between kernels
- Small dark pycnidia specks

This matches the test image well:
- Same tan/straw-colored rotted kernels
- White-gray mycelium concentrated at center and between kernels
- Visible dark specks (pycnidia characteristic of Diplodia/Stenocarpella)
- The end cross-section view clearly shows the typical Diplodia rot pattern spreading from the base inward
